title: NHS diabetic eye screening: retinopathy and maculopathy grading
text: The NHS Diabetic Eye Screening Programme grades retinopathy as R0 when there is none and R1 for background retinopathy, which includes microaneurysms, retinal haemorrhages and any exudate. R2 is pre proliferative retinopathy: venous beading, a venous loop or reduplication, intraretinal microvascular abnormality (IRMA) or multiple deep, round or blot haemorrhages. R3A is active proliferative retinopathy: new vessels on the disc or elsewhere, preretinal or vitreous haemorrhage, or preretinal fibrosis with or without tractional retinal detachment, and reactivation in a previously treated eye. R3S is stable treated proliferative retinopathy. M1 maculopathy is graded for exudate within one disc diameter of the centre of the fovea, a group of exudates within the macula, retinal thickening within one disc diameter of the fovea where stereo viewing is available, or any microaneurysm or haemorrhage within one disc diameter of the fovea only when best visual acuity is 6/12 or worse. Otherwise the maculopathy grade is M0. An ungradable image is graded U.

title: NHS diabetic eye screening pathways: grading, referral and surveillance
text: People aged 12 and over with two consecutive negative screening results are screened every 24 months. People with a single negative result or a positive non referable result are screened every 12 months. R2, R3A and R3S results are referable to the hospital eye service, and people referred are suspended from routine digital screening. R1M1 results are usually kept in digital surveillance run by the screening programme. Ungradable images are repeated on another date, and if a digital image cannot be obtained the person is moved to slit lamp biomicroscopy surveillance, which is also used for more frequent monitoring such as every 3 or 6 months or screening in pregnancy. The programme ranks outcomes for the eye needing action most urgently in this order: R3AM1, R3AM0, R3SM1, R2M1, R1M1, R2M0, U, R3SM0, R1M0 and R0M0.
